newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. prepares to take missile engines outside Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.N. prepares to take missile engines outside Iraq.

text.p: United Nations experts are packing scrapped missile engines to remove them outside Iraq for examination, a U.N. source said on Sunday.
"The packing is going on...preparations are underway to remove them," the source told Reuters.
Asked where the approximately 100 destroyed engines would be moved to, he said: "I do not know yet."

Iraq and the United Nations Special Commission (UNSCOM), in charge of ridding Iraqi weapons of mass destruction, agreed last week to remove the missile remnants either to the United States or France for analysis. Earlier Iraq had objected to remove them to the United States and suggested Russia or France instead.

The United Nations wants to establish if scrapped parts that Iraq had said it destroyed and buried soon after the 1991 Gulf War, are from missing Soviet-made engines as Iraq maintained or are local equipment to divert attention from hidden missile engines.

UNSCOM's chairman Rolf Ekeus must certify Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift curbs on Iraqi oil exports, although Baghdad is allowing limited oil exports under a humanitarian deal.
Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Friday his government gave Ekeus data to prove it no longer has banned missiles in its arsenal.
